payload.statement: The Thr45Met substitution sits on the WH1 surface that contacts WIP, so the bulkier, hydrophobic Met side chain disrupts the WASP–WIP interface without changing the fold.
payload.would_refute: Residue 45 in PDB 9S9X (WASP/WIP complex) has no atom within about 5 Å of any WIP atom, and modelling Met at position 45 in that complex leaves the interface contacts and buried surface area unchanged.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Only residue-specific structural evidence is E15, which observes residue 45 in a WASP/WIP complex, so the residue is at least near a binding partner. This is observation, not proof of contact. The stability scores (E7, E9, E10, E13) are generic to the protein and do not separate fold effects from interface effects. Missing: contact distances in 9S9X, any measured Thr45Met binding or folding data (G1, G4).

payload.statement: The Thr45Met substitution destabilises the WH1 β-sandwich core: Thr45 packs against neighbouring hydrophobic residues, and the larger Met side chain causes steric clash that lowers folding stability and reduces the fraction of properly folded protein.
payload.would_refute: In the AlphaFold model AF-P42768-F1 and in 9S9X, residue 45 is solvent-exposed (relative accessibility above about 40%) and a Thr-to-Met model with local relaxation gives a predicted stability change under 1 kcal/mol with no change in neighbouring backbone or side-chain positions.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Several predictors (AlphaMissense 0.59, EVE 0.68, popEVE -4.3, conservation 0.62) point to damage, and the neighbouring WH1 mutants L46P and A47D are stable in a complementation assay (E11), which makes a fold-level effect plausible. However, none of these scores is residue-specific structure or stability data, and the neighbouring-residue result does not show that Thr45 is buried. Missing: burial and per-residue ΔΔG for T45M (G2, G6).

payload.statement: Thr45 is part of the WH1 intramolecular contact that holds WASP in its autoinhibited (closed) conformation; the Thr45Met side chain shifts this contact so the protein favours the open state, which changes the shape of the fold without destabilising it.
payload.would_refute: In the AlphaFold model and in any closed-state WASP structure, residue 45 has no side-chain contact within about 4 Å with residues of the GBD, CRIB or other non-WH1 domains, and the Thr45Met model shows no change in the WH1–GBD distance or inter-domain angle.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The only evidence on the conformational state (E11) concerns L46P and A47D, not Thr45 or Thr45Met, and it is a bimolecular complementation assay rather than a structure. E16 is general. The hypothesis is included because it is a distinct class and the question asks about shape. It ranks last because no retrieved source puts residue 45 at an inter-domain contact. Missing: a closed-state WASP structure and inter-domain contact data (G2).

payload.summary: Three agent-generated hypotheses for Thr45Met are recorded: protein_interaction (rank 1, WIP-interface disruption, supported by residue 45 being observed in the 9S9X WASP/WIP complex), stability_folding (rank 2, core packing clash, supported by generic damaging predictions and neighbouring WH1 stability data), and domain_interface (rank 3, shift of the autoinhibitory WH1 contact, weakly supported). Runner should test each with the refutation criteria on AF-P42768-F1 and 9S9X: contact distances to WIP, relative accessibility and ΔΔG for T45M, and inter-domain contacts. payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change for Thr45Met on the AlphaFold model of P42768, plus pLDDT at residue 45 and the same predictor for other substitutions at that residue. Discriminates H2 (destabilising core clash) from H1 and H3 (fold unchanged).
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising value at or above the threshold would move H2 up and weaken H1 and H3, which both assume the fold is unchanged. A neutral value would weaken H2 and leave H1 and H3 standing, so the ranking would be reshuffled but not settled. The test does not measure shape directly and FoldX has errors near 1 kcal/mol, and G2 leaves burial of residue 45 unknown, so the outcome is only moderately decisive.

per_hypothesis.why: T1 is a stability (folding free energy) test. It does not measure WIP contacts, so it does not bear on the WASP/WIP interface claim. The FoldX value of +3.56 kcal/mol says nothing about binding. H1 still rests on E15, E4, E5, E8 and E9, none of which measured an interface contact at residue 45.

FoldX ddG for T45M is +3.56 kcal/mol on AF-P42768-F1, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, with residue pLDDT 96.62 (T1). H2's refutation criterion was a solvent-exposed site with a predicted change under 1 kcal/mol. The measured value is 3.56, so that criterion is not met. The control T45R gave +7.43 kcal/mol, which fits a larger penalty for a bigger substitution at the same site. This adds direct stability evidence to E7, E9, E10, E13, E18, E11 and E3.

H3 says the substitution changes shape 'without destabilising it'. T1 measured a destabilising ddG of +3.56 kcal/mol, which goes against that clause. H3's refutation criterion concerns GBD/CRIB contact distances, which T1 did not measure, so H3 is weakened and not refuted. Missense3d returned 'Neutral' (T1), but that is a weak, separate signal and does not offset the FoldX value.

payload.uncertainty: FoldX on a predicted model has errors near 1 kcal/mol, so +3.56 is a clear signal but not a precise magnitude. The result is a single predictor with no repeat or relaxation step, and the FoldX job returned no ID or manifest, so it is not independently reproducible from the record beyond the stored T1 values. Controls passed: pLDDT 96.62 at residue 45 (applicable), and the within-site comparison T45R +7.43 shows the predictor scales with substitution severity. A stability value alone cannot separate H2 from an interface effect, so H1 remains untested. The test does not measure the fold itself, so it cannot confirm a shape change (H3) or a lower folded fraction in cells. Validation still needed: relaxed or repeated FoldX, relative accessibility and neighbour packing at residue 45, and an experimental stability or expression measurement for T45M."

## Question
Does p.Thr45Met in WASP (WAS, P42768) change the folded shape of the protein? The record answers this only with computational predictions. No measured fold comparison was run [T3].

## Evidence
ClinVar classes the variant as Pathogenic, with criteria provided and no conflicts [E1]. UniProt lists it as a natural variant of moderate impact [E2]. Residue 45 lies in the WH1 domain [E3, E4]. The AlphaFold DB model AF-P42768-F1 has a mean pLDDT of 69.38 [E18], and residue 45 has pLDDT 96.62 [T1]. No retrieved paper measures the folding or structure of Thr45Met itself [G1]. One experimental WASP/WIP complex (9S9X) observes residue 45 [E15].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (agent-generated hypothesis, protein interaction) proposes that the substitution disrupts the WIP interface without changing the fold [H1]. H2 (stability) proposes core destabilisation [H2]. H3 (domain interface) proposes a shift in autoinhibition [H3]. Starting ranks were H1, H2, H3 [H1, H2, H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
Round 1: T1 (stability, learning 0.55, no approval) was chosen over T2 (structural context) and T3 (structure comparison, learning 0.7 but feasibility 0.2, approval needed, blocked) [T1, T2, T3]. Safety cleared T1 [decision seq 43].
Round 2, reopened because the favourite changed: T2 was chosen to separate H1 from H2. T3 and T4 were rejected [T2, T4].

## Result
T1: FoldX predicts a ΔΔG of +3.56 kcal/mol for Thr45Met, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold. The control T45R gave +7.43 kcal/mol [T1, E20, E21]. T2: residue 45 lies in two predicted pockets (buriedness 0.74 and 0.79) and in no predicted protein-protein interface [T2, E22, E23]. These are predictions only and have not been validated experimentally.

## Updated decision
Round 1: H1 was favoured before T1 and H2 after. The decision changed [decision seq 55]. Round 2: H2 stayed favoured, H1 was weakened and H3 was weakened [decision seq 77]. H2 is the favourite now, provisionally.

## Candidates
The lab's decision is that a drug could act on the H2 mechanism through a pathway node, BTK [G7]. The translator returned four pathway_node rows via BTK, each with two bridge steps [G7]. Every direction check read unknown, so the direction filter rejected all four and none matched or opposed [G7]. Safety cleared 0 of 4 [G8]. No candidate was recorded. Any candidate would be a Helix hypothesis, not a recommendation.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
T1 is a single FoldX predictor on a predicted model, with roughly 1 kcal/mol error and no relaxation step [T1]. T2 used a monomer model and predicted pockets, not measured binding sites [T2]. The fold itself was not compared. T3 is blocked because its provider is down and it needs approval [T3]. The direction of WAS activity is unresolved [G7]. Nothing has been validated experimentally.

## Next experiment
Test H1's refutation criterion on the 9S9X complex: distances from residue 45 to WIP and the effect of a modelled Met [next_experiments seq 78]. Also run relative accessibility and relaxed FoldX to test H2 [next_experiments seq 56]. Run the fold comparison (T3) once a provider is available and approved.
